What changed

  • One scheme explains about half of the increase.

    Payments labelled Our City Our River, Package 2 rose by £14.7m, from £2.0m to £16.7m, mostly to John Sisk & Son Limited. Without that line, total spend is up about 4.6% instead of 9.3%.

  • Children’s services and childcare funding are the other main driver.

    Children & Young People rose £14.0m (+13%), led by Special Schools (+£4.3m), Agency Residential (+£4.3m) and working parent funding (+£3.4m). Homelessness rose £2.9m (+95%).

  • Spend with larger companies grew. Spend with small firms did not.

    Suppliers classed as “Company” received £89.5m, up £32.5m (+57.0%). Spend with SMEs was £162.9m, against £163.3m last year (−0.2%), and with public bodies it fell 3.5%. There were more payments, but the typical payment was smaller.

Read directorate and department changes with care. Housing & Regulatory Services appears from December 2025 with £16.7m this year and nothing last year. “Adults Health and Housing” fell by £15.8m over the same period, and its £16.7m last year is almost the same size as the new department’s figure. The change may reflect how departments are organised rather than new spending. Directorate figures below are shown as published, after grouping older directorate names under today’s.
